summary: This work develops a closed-form method to calculate logical error rates $L$ for surface codes by recursively counting minimum-length logical paths (MLLPs) containing $d_e = (d+1)/2$ errors, avoiding expensive decoder simulations. The approach proves accurate when $pd^2 \ll 1$ and provides rigorous bounds for the regime $pd^2 \gtrsim 1$, and is extended to locally and globally correlated error models plus measurement errors.
motivation: Designing practical quantum computers requires rapidly evaluating logical error rates across many combinations of physical error rate $p$ and code distance $d$, but current methods rely on computationally prohibitive Monte Carlo simulations or inaccurate extrapolation from sparse experimental data.
method: The authors exploit topological constraints of surface codes to enumerate error configurations via dynamic programming (Algorithm 1 with memoization), computing $C_{d_e}$ exactly for unrotated codes as $d\binom{d}{d_e}$ and for rotated codes via path-counting with geometric constraints from Theorem 2; results are combined with binomial probabilities in Equation~1 and bounded by Theorem 1 to achieve provably accurate $L$ estimates in polynomial runtime.
result: For unrotated codes, $C_{d_e} \approx \frac{d_e}{\pi}4^{d_e}$ and logical error scaling matches $L \approx A(p/p_\mathrm{th})^{d_e}$ with $p_\mathrm{th} \approx 1.22 \times 10^{-2}$ ($R^2 = 1 - 6.3 \times 10^{-6}$); rotated codes achieve $p_\mathrm{th} \approx 7.3 \times 10^{-2}$ but require only $\approx 75\%$ of the qubits for equivalent fidelity.
